checkpoint: 1 — hypothesis verified before touching a font-size number
hypothesis: The tooltip popup HudButton._MakeCustomTooltip returns is not a descendant of the HUD's own scaled Control subtree (_hudRoot), so it cannot inherit _hudRoot.Scale the way every other HUD label does, and its literal font sizes stay the same physical size while the rest of the interface grows with UiScale.

structuralEvidence.claim: Before this change, HudButton._MakeCustomTooltip set the tooltip's font sizes and width as literal integers with no reference to any scale variable, so they could not have varied with UiScale regardless of how the popup is parented.
structuralEvidence.source: git show ff6d679:src/DungeonFortress.Game/HudButton.cs (the tree the owner's playtest and Issue #127 were taken from)

structuralEvidence.claim: Main.LayoutHud scales the rest of the HUD by setting _hudRoot.Scale, a Control-level 2D transform. Every Label/Button that is an actual descendant of _hudRoot renders through that transform automatically.

Godot 4.7's own engine source shows the tooltip popup is never added as a child of the hovered control's ancestor Control tree: it is wrapped in a PopupPanel (a Window) and parented directly under the hovered control itself, bypassing _hudRoot's Scale.

A Window scales its own content by content_scale_factor, computed from get_popup_base_transform(), which is unrelated to any ambient Control.Scale a game applies manually. This project's own stretch configuration (canvas_items + aspect=expand) keeps that base transform's scale at 1 for any window size, because 'expand' exposes more of the design frame instead of stretching it — so popup_scale is 1 regardless of window size in this project, and the tooltip has no ambient scale to pick up from either mechanism.

liveMeasurement.command: .artifacts/evidence-127.ps1 (dot-sources scripts/GodotTools.ps1, invokes Godot 4.7.1 console directly with --headless --resolution <frame> --path src/DungeonFortress.Game -- --smoke --fixture baseline --tile-size 40 --camera-position 560,320 --ui-scale <scale> --frame-size <frame>, then parses the printed godot_headless_smoke JSON event's view.hudReadability.texts)
liveMeasurement.note: Measured AFTER the fix: HudButton.MakeAuthoredTooltip keeps an invisible sample of the tooltip as a permanent child of _hudRoot (Main.CreateControlStrips), so it now appears in hudReadability.texts under the names Label[TooltipTitle] / Label[TooltipBody]. physicalPixels = logicalPixels * this run's own UiScale, exactly the same formula HudReadability.PhysicalTextPixels applies to every other HUD text.
liveMeasurement.interpretation: The tooltip's reported physical size grows exactly in step with UiScale (10/12 at 1.0, 15/18 at 1.5, 20/24 at 2.0), matching HudFontSizes.ScaledSize's own arithmetic (DungeonFortress.Presentation.Tests.HudFontSizesTests.Scaled_size_grows_exactly_with_UI_scale). Frame/UiScale pairs were chosen so the logical frame (frame / uiScale) never drops below the project's own 1024x720 minimum (scripts/run-game.ps1's $minimumLogicalWidth/$minimumLogicalHeight): 1280x720 at 1.0 (logical 1280x720), 1920x1080 at 1.5 (logical 1280x720), 2048x1440 at 2.0 (logical 1024x720).

conclusion: The hypothesis holds. The fix accordingly changes where the tooltip's size comes from (HudButton.UiScale, kept in step with Main.LayoutHud's uiScale, applied inside HudButton.BuildTooltip via HudFontSizes.ScaledSize) rather than only raising the two literal font-size numbers, and gives the readability guard a permanent, invisible sample of the tooltip inside the scaled HUD subtree (Main.CreateControlStrips) rather than trying to read a popup that only exists on hover.
